reviews.comment: took him last semester for game theory and he's great! curves his exams substantially so you're guaranteed at least a B if you do the homeworks and answer all the questions on the exams, since hw is graded on participation and there's a lot of partial credit given on exams.

Class is hard, but if you put in the effort, you'll pass. Homeworks are graded on participation. Cheet sheets are allowed for exams. Professor and TA provide good feedback and are accessible outside class. Extra credit opportunities and an optional final exam. Got a grade over 100 even though I didn't fully understand the material.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is hard, but if you put in the effort, you'll pass. Attendance optional. Homeworks are more graded by participation. Professor and TAs give good feedback and are accessible outside class. A lot of extra credit opportunities and final cumulative exam is optional. Got a grade over 100 even though I didn't fully understand the material
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The hardest class I have taken, Super smart professor but needs to dumb it down a little for class. He curves the crap out of tests which is super kind and nice, pretty hard to not get a D for credit. However, if you are going to law school, I'd wait till your last semester in case you suck at math, that way it is not on your transcript.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A very difficult subject, he doesn't know how to teach those who have no background in game theory. This class is exceedingly difficult for a course that is required but is called an intro. to game theory course. TAMU needs to restructure this course but in general not awful prof, disorganized and curves test grades, Changed test format 3 times.

Looking at old reviews and he's definitely cleaned up his act since then. 30% per exam (including final), lowest grade dropped and all are massively curved. Homework is 10% and essentially completion. Ended with above a 100. Material is difficult but prof and TA are helpful (also using Game Theory videos on YouTube by William Spaniel).
needs to learn how to teach

Dr. Malis is one of the best professors I have ever had at A&M. He is super approachable and will go the extra mile, but you have to put in the effort and show him you care. He will help you with everything. The class is super hard, but it can be accomplished if you try and get help. He does go fast in lectures, but you can always ask questions.
This is class is one of the hardest in poli-sci. But it might not be the instructor's fault but the course's. Dr. Malis is super responsive and try to help us to follow the class materials.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Malis has no idea how to teach. He intentionally makes tests so hard (& tells the class he does), that the average is a 30. I studied for 30+ hours on each exam and still never chose an answer I knew was 100% correct. Exams are select all with 6-8 choices. The TAs also have no idea what is going on and often give students the wrong information.

Professor Malis curved the exams, despite them being really hard, it was clear he wanted to help students. He was always available outside of class and responds quickly. He doesn't provide exam reviews or a clear idea of what to expect in terms of content on the exams which made it difficult to prepare for. Lecture was also bit difficult to follow.

He's a smart guy but not a good teacher. He can't communicate the topics in an effective way where you can actually understand the material. The exams were impossible and he told us that he intentionally made them more difficult than necessary. Take this class with ANY other professor.

He does not understand how to explain topics to normal people. The mean score on every exam was around a 30. He writes in the exam instructions that he knows you will not be able to complete the difficulty of all the questions in the given amount of time. Be prepared to feel inadequate. Unless you study for hours you will not pass the class.

The tests are nearly impossible. My class averages ranged from 25-30 for the three exams before the curve. The exams made many of us feel badly about ourselves but it is not our fault. The homework is difficult but doable. Take another professor if you can.

I want to first say that professor Malis is not a bad guy. Professor Malis was not prepared to teach such a complex topic. He is very smart but does not know how to dumb it down enough for undergrad students to understand. I would never recommend anyone to take his class.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy
